name: hyp-37-half-split
comment: SPLIT COUNTERPART of hyp-37-half: every edge that is exactly TWICE another carries a flat 180-degree corner at its midpoint, so one tile's side may be met by two. The {3,7} edge is EXACTLY twice the half — cosh(edge) = 2 cosh(half)^2 - 1 — so it carries a flat 180-degree corner at its midpoint and may be met by TWO neighbours. ⚑ This retires the parity prediction the unsplit palette states: the argument that no {3,7} vertex can be left uncut assumed each corner is flanked by one FULL edge and one HALF-edge and that the two must alternate round an odd vertex. With the full edge split there are no full edges left to alternate, so tilings below k=6 are no longer excluded and finding them is the point of this board. Halving a regular tile always produces this ratio — the cut lands on a midpoint, and arc length is additive along a geodesic, in H^2 and on the sphere exactly as in the plane (AL, 2026-08-18). The unsplit board sees only the tilings where every edge is matched whole; this one is a SUPERSET of it, so containment is the check to run. Angles unchanged apart from the flats, which is why the curvature is too: a flat corner adds D/2 to the angle sum and 1 to n, and (n-2)*D/2 grows by exactly the same D/2, so the tile's area is untouched. HALF THE {3,7} TRIANGLE. In the hyperbolic {3,7} tiling seven triangles meet at every vertex, so each corner is 360/7 degrees; an altitude cuts one into two triangles with angles pi/2, pi/7 and 2pi/7 — 90, 180/7 and 360/7 degrees. Scalene, so CHIRAL, and so the mirror image is its own alphabet symbol; this palette runs only because of the sided-classes repair. Its sides are the {3,7} edge, half of it and the altitude — three edge types — and the edge is EXACTLY twice the half, which is what cosh(2x) = 2cosh(x)^2 - 1 says about the two: cosh(half) = 1.152389 and cosh(edge) = 1.656027 = 2(1.152389)^2 - 1. D=28 because that is the smallest ring holding all three angles: 180/7 = 2 units of 2pi/28, 360/7 = 4, and 90 = 7. They sum to 13 against the 14 a flat triangle would, so the deficit is 1 unit = 90/7 degrees, which is the tile's area.
